deploy-bot: :rotating_light: pipeline failed - service=search build=2026.03.15-rc stage=deploy canary started but healthcheck failing (5xx spike). reason=image-digest-mismatch. logs: 'expected sha256:abcd1234 got sha256:fff111'

Samir Jain: saw the alert, pulling logs + metrics. canary is ~10% of traffic, 4.7% 5xx on search-api-canary. attaching quick grep from deploy job:
```
> pushing image registry.redwood.ai/search:2026.03.15-rc
> manifest digest: sha256:fff111
> verifying deployed digest == expected sha256:abcd1234
> mismatch -> mark deployment unstable
```

Leah Chen: ugh, looks like the CI published a different image than the one the deploy job expected. possibly cache/index mismatch in the build pipeline. Do we have a quick kill switch for the ranking change?

Omar Patel: we do. recommend flip feature flag `search-new-ranking` off for all traffic immediately, then rollback canary to previous image SHA. flag path: featureflags.prod.redwood.ai

Kai Morgan: taking the flag. running:`curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $FF_SVC_TOKEN' -d '{"flag":"search-new-ranking","value":false,"env":"prod"}' https://featureflags.prod.redwood.ai/flags/toggle`

Kai Morgan: done. :white_check_mark: flag is false. response: `\{"status":"ok","flag":"search-new-ranking","value":false\}`

Samir Jain: good. Leah/Om, can we do immediate rollback of the canary to the previous stable image (sha256:abcd1234)? command I plan to run:`kubectl -n prod set image deploy/search search=registry.redwood.ai/search@sha256:abcd1234 --record` then scale up stable and scale down canary. Anyone object?

Leah Chen: do it. Also open a quick ticket to CS so they can triage customer impact and communications. Marta?

Marta (CS Liaison): on it. will draft a proactive note to customers who saw errors (search failures) and track affected orgs. ETA 20m.

Samir Jain: executing rollback now. log:
```
$ kubectl -n prod set image deploy/search search=registry.redwood.ai/search@sha256:abcd1234 --record
deployment.apps/search image updated
waiting for rollout to complete...
rollout status deployment/search: success
```

Samir Jain: canary 5xx dropped to baseline (~0.1%) after rollback. monitoring for 20m.

Leah Chen: root cause hypothesis: CI reused a cached intermediate layer which had a tag reused across builds; tag-based verification expected the digest for tag `2026.03.15-rc` but image registry had a different digest due to race between two pipeline runs. Essentially cache poisoning in our ephemeral builder images.

Omar Patel: yep — reproducible locally by forcing cache hit. the digest in the deploy job is looked up prior to pushing and then again on the cluster, mismatch happens when a concurrent build pushes same tag with different content. we should never rely on mutable tags for deploy verification.

Kai Morgan: immediate mitigations:
- Invalidate/Clear ephemeral builder cache for the pipeline run (done for current run)
- Change deploy job to use immutable digests only (use `image@sha256:...`) rather than tag on K8s update
- Add a verification step in CI that compares pushed digest to the deploy-time digest and fail the pipeline if they differ
- Prevent reuse of short-lived tags: append build-id to tag (already in plan) or require `--no-cache` for critical release pipeline

Leah Chen: plan for this incident (short):
1) rollback complete & verify (Samir) — done, monitoring
2) feature flag off (Kai) — done
3) purge/lock the `2026.03.15-rc` tag in registry to prevent accidental reuse (Samir)
4) create follow-up ticket to harden pipeline (Omar/Leah)
5) postmortem and code change (CI) before next rollout

Samir Jain: purged tag and re-tagged stable image as `search:stable` and pinned digest. command used: `gcloud container images add-tag registry.redwood.ai/search@sha256:abcd1234 registry.redwood.ai/search:stable --quiet`

Omar Patel: creating GH issue now: "CI: verify pushed image digest, avoid mutable tags" with checklist (immutable tags, no-cache option, digest-compare step, registry lock). linking to incident doc.

Marta (CS Liaison): customer impact summary for postmortem: ~2.3% of requests across 50 orgs experienced transient search failures during canary window (~12m). no data loss. draft ready for review.

oncall-rotation: tagging next oncall for handoff — Omar, you'll take this for PM and follow-ups. Samir — please add notes to incident board and hand off at 1718012000.

Omar Patel: acknowledged, taking ownership for remediation and postmortem. I'll coordinate with infra to land the CI changes and make the digest verification mandatory.

Samir Jain: quick logs to attach to incident: deploy job stdout, registry push events, k8s rollout events. I'll upload to the incident doc.

Leah Chen: add tests to our canary gating too: gate by digest-equality check and require zero 5xx before advancing to 50% traffic.

deploy-bot: Incident created: REDWOOD-INC-2026-142 (sev=2) — oncall assigned: Omar Patel — incident doc: https://redwood-internal/incident/REDWOOD-INC-2026-142

Marta (CS Liaison): sending customer note now. will post updates in #customer-notifications when sent.

Samir Jain: handoff: logging out at 1718012000 — Omar has the lead. leaving runbook steps in incident doc. good work team :thumbsup:

Omar Patel: will run RCA and publish within 72h. thanks everyone for quick flip of the flag and rollback. :pray:
